sanskrit: nagaraṃ caiva deśaṃ ca rakṣobalasamanvitaḥ tatkṛte paracakrāc ca bhūtebhyaś ca na no bhayam
english: Attended by the power of that demon, both the city and the country are protected — because of him we have no fear from enemy armies or from spirits.

sanskrit: vetanaṃ tasya vihitaṃ śālivāhasya bhojanam mahiṣau puruṣaś caiko yas tad ādāya gacchati
english: His appointed wage has been fixed: a cartload of rice, two buffaloes, and a single man — whoever carries that food goes to him.

sanskrit: ekaikaś caiva puruṣas tat prayacchati bhojanam sa vāro bahubhir varṣair bhavaty asutaro naraiḥ
english: Each family in turn delivers that food; the rotation comes around again only after many years, yet it costs men their lives — a burden impossible to bear.

sanskrit: tadvimokṣāya ye cāpi yatante puruṣāḥ kva cit saputradārāṃs tān hatvā tad rakṣo bhakṣayaty uta
english: And those men who have anywhere tried to liberate themselves from this — the demon has killed them together with their wives and children and devoured them.

sanskrit: vetrakīyagṛhe rājā nāyaṃ nayam ihāsthitaḥ anāmayaṃ janasyāsya yena syād adya śāśvatam
english: The king dwelling in the Vetrakīya house has not adopted a policy here by which the lasting welfare of these people could be assured today.

sanskrit: etadarhā vayaṃ nūnaṃ vasāmo durbalasya ye viṣaye nityam udvignāḥ kurājānam upāśritāḥ
english: We who live under the dominion of this weak man, constantly full of dread, sheltering under a bad king — we deserve precisely this fate.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kasya vaktavyāḥ kasya vā chandacāriṇaḥ guṇair ete hi vāsyante kāmagāḥ pakṣiṇo yathā
english: To whom should brahmins speak, or those who wander as they please? These men of virtue are tamed by their own good qualities, like free-flying birds caught in a snare.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ prathamaṃ vindet tato bhāryāṃ tato dhanam trayasya saṃcaye cāsya jñātīn putrāṃś ca dhārayet
english: One should first find a king, then a wife, then wealth; and when those three are secured, one can then support one's kinsmen and children.

sanskrit: viparītaṃ mayā cedaṃ trayaṃ sarvam upārjitam ta imām āpadaṃ prāpya bhṛśaṃ tapsyāmahe vayam
english: But I have acquired all three of these in the wrong order — and having now reached this calamity, we shall suffer greatly.

sanskrit: so 'yam asmān anuprāpto vāraḥ kulavināśanaḥ bhojanaṃ puruṣaś caikaḥ pradeyaṃ vetanaṃ mayā
english: This turn — the destroyer of our family — has now come round to us; I must deliver as his wage one man along with the food.

sanskrit: na ca me vidyate vittaṃ saṃkretuṃ puruṣaṃ kva cit suhṛjjanaṃ pradātuṃ ca na śakṣyāmi kathaṃ cana gatiṃ cāpi na paśyāmi tasmān mokṣāya rakṣasaḥ
english: I have no money anywhere to purchase a man, nor can I in any way give a friend; I see no way of escape from that demon.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ duḥkhārṇave magno mahaty asutare bhṛśam sahaivaitair gamiṣyāmi bāndhavair adya rākṣasam tato naḥ sahitan kṣudraḥ sarvān evopabhokṣyati
english: Sunk thus deeply in this vast, uncrossable ocean of grief, I shall go today together with these relatives to the demon — and then that wretched creature will devour all of us together.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca na viṣādas tvayā kāryo bhayād asmāt kathaṃ cana upāyaḥ paridṛṣṭo 'tra tasmān mokṣāya rakṣasaḥ
english: Kuntī said: You must not give way to despair or to any fear on our account — a means of deliverance from that demon has been perceived here.

sanskrit: ekas tava suto bālaḥ kanyā caikā tapasvinī na te tayos tathā patnyā gamanaṃ tatra rocaye
english: You have one young son, one ascetic daughter, and your wife — I do not favour the going of any of those three there.

sanskrit: mama pañca sutā brahmaṃs teṣām eko gamiṣyati tvadarthaṃ balim ādāya tasya pāpasya rakṣasaḥ
english: I have five sons, O brahmin; one of them shall go on your behalf, carrying the food-offering for that wicked demon.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca nāham etat kariṣyāmi jīvitārthī kathaṃ cana brāhmaṇasyātitheś caiva svārthe prāṇair viyojanam
english: The brahmin said: I will not do this — not for my own life's sake, not under any circumstances — this severing of a brahmin guest from his life for my own benefit.

sanskrit: na tv etad akulīnāsu nādharmiṣṭhāsu vidyate yad brāhmaṇārthe visṛjed ātmānam api cātmajam
english: Not even among those of ignoble birth or unrighteous conduct is such a thing found — that one would sacrifice oneself or one's own child for the sake of a brahmin.

sanskrit: ātmanas tu mayā śreyo boddhavyam iti rocaye brahmavadhyātmavadhyā vā śreya ātmavadho mama
english: I hold it my duty to seek my own good; and whether it be the sin of killing a brahmin or the killing of myself, the death of myself is better for me.

sanskrit: brahmavadhyā paraṃ pāpaṃ niṣkṛtir nātra vidyate abuddhipūrvaṃ kṛtvāpi śreya ātmavadho mama
english: The killing of a brahmin is the supreme sin, and there is no expiation for it; even if done without prior intent, my own death is better for me.

sanskrit: na tv ahaṃ vadham ākāṅkṣe svayam evātmanaḥ śubhe paraiḥ kṛte vadhe pāpaṃ na kiṃ cin mayi vidyate
english: Yet I do not myself desire my own death, O auspicious one — when death is brought about by others, no sin whatsoever falls on me.

sanskrit: abhisaṃdhikṛte tasmin brāhmaṇasya vadhe mayā niṣkṛtiṃ na prapaśyāmi nṛśaṃsaṃ kṣudram eva ca
english: In the deliberate killing of a brahmin by me I see no expiation; it is both cruel and base.

sanskrit: āgatasya gṛhe tyāgas tathaiva śaraṇārthinaḥ yācamānasya ca vadho nṛśaṃsaṃ paramaṃ matam
english: To abandon one who has come to one's house, likewise one who has sought shelter, and to cause the death of one who is supplicating — these are considered the ultimate cruelty.

sanskrit: kuryān na ninditaṃ karma na nṛśaṃsaṃ kadā cana iti pūrve mahātmāna āpaddharmavido viduḥ
english: "One should never perform a censurable or cruel act" — so the great-souled men of former times, who knew the dharma of emergencies, have declared.

sanskrit: śreyāṃs tu sahadārasya vināśo 'dya mama svayam brāhmaṇasya vadhaṃ nāham anumaṃsye kathaṃ cana
english: But my own destruction today, together with my wife, is better — I will not in any way consent to the killing of a brahmin.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca mamāpy eṣā matir brahman viprā rakṣyā iti sthirā na cāpy aniṣṭaḥ putro me yadi putraśataṃ bhavet
english: Kuntī said: My own resolve too is firm, O brahmin — brahmins must be protected; nor would a son be unwanted by me even if I had a hundred sons.

sanskrit: na cāsau rākṣasaḥ śakto mama putravināśane vīryavān mantrasiddhaś ca tejasvī ca suto mama
english: And that demon is not capable of destroying my son — my son is mighty, accomplished through sacred formulas, and full of blazing energy.

sanskrit: rākṣasāya ca tat sarvaṃ prāpayiṣyati bhojanam mokṣayiṣyati cātmānam iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: He will deliver all that food to the demon and will free himself — such is my firm conviction.

sanskrit: samāgatāś ca vīreṇa dṛṣṭapūrvāś ca rākṣasāḥ balavanto mahākāyā nihatāś cāpy anekaśaḥ
english: For demons — powerful, huge-bodied — have met that hero before and have been seen by him, and many have been slain by him.

sanskrit: na tv idaṃ keṣu cid brahman vyāhartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana vidyārthino hi me putrān viprakuryuḥ kutūhalāt
english: But this must not be told to anyone at all, O brahmin — for those in pursuit of learning would, out of curiosity, interfere with my sons.

sanskrit: guruṇā cānanujñāto grāhayed yaṃ suto mama na sa kuryāt tayā kāryaṃ vidyayeti satāṃ matam
english: "That son of mine who has not been released by his guru should not employ that power" — such is the view of the righteous.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu pṛthayā sa vipro bhāryayā saha hṛṣṭaḥ saṃpūjayām āsa tad vākyam amṛtopamam
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus addressed by Pṛthā, that brahmin together with his wife, rejoicing, honoured her speech as equal to nectar.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntī ca vipraś ca sahitāv anilātmajam tam abrūtāṃ kuruṣveti sa tathety abravīc ca tau
english: Then Kuntī and the brahmin together addressed the son of the Wind: "Do it" — and he answered them: "So be it."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kariṣya iti bhīmena pratijñāte tu bhārata ājagmus te tataḥ sarve bhaikṣam ādāya pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: When Bhīma had pledged "I shall do it," O descendant of Bharata, all the Pāṇḍavas then returned, having collected their alms.

sanskrit: ākāreṇaiva taṃ jñātvā pāṇḍuputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ rahaḥ samupaviśyaikas tataḥ papraccha mātaram
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu, reading the situation from Bhīma's very bearing, sat apart alone and then questioned his mother.

sanskrit: kiṃ cikīrṣaty ayaṃ karma bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ bhavaty anumate kaccid ayaṃ kartum ihecchati
english: "What deed does this Bhīma of terrible valour intend to do? Is this that he wishes to do here done with your consent?"

sanskrit: kunty uvāca mamaiva vacanād eṣa kariṣyati paraṃtapaḥ brāhmaṇārthe mahat kṛtyaṃ moṣkāya nagarasya ca
english: Kuntī said: At my own bidding this scorcher of foes will perform a great deed — for the sake of the brahmin and for the deliverance of the city.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kim idaṃ sāhasaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ bhavatyā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam parityāgaṃ hi putrasya na praśaṃsanti sādhavaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What rash and reckless wrong has been done by you? Good men do not praise the abandonment of a son.

sanskrit: kathaṃ parasutasyārthe svasutaṃ tyaktum icchasi lokavṛttiviruddhaṃ vai putratyāgāt kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: How can you wish to abandon your own son for the sake of another's? What you have done by giving up a son is contrary to the practice of the world.

sanskrit: yasya bāhū samāśritya sukhaṃ sarve svapāmahe rājyaṃ cāpahṛtaṃ kṣudrair ājihīrṣāmahe punaḥ
english: Relying on whose arms we all sleep in comfort — it is by relying on them that we hope to win back the kingdom stolen by wicked men.

sanskrit: yasya duryodhano vīryaṃ cintayann amitaujasaḥ na śete vasatīḥ sarvā duḥkhāc chakuninā saha
english: Thinking on whose valour — his, of boundless might — Duryodhana spends all his nights sleepless with grief, together with Śakuni.

sanskrit: yasya vīrasya vīryeṇa muktā jatugṛhād vayam anyebhyaś caiva pāpebhyo nihataś ca purocanaḥ
english: By the valour of this hero we were freed from the house of lac; and from other wicked men too, and Purоcana was slain.

sanskrit: yasya vīryaṃ samāśritya vasupūrṇāṃ vasuṃdharām imāṃ manyāmahe prāptāṃ nihatya dhṛtarāṣṭrajān
english: Relying on whose might we think it possible to gain this earth full of riches — after slaying the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tasya vyavasitas tyāgo buddhim āsthāya kāṃ tvayā kaccin na duḥkhair buddhis te viplutā gatacetasaḥ
english: Resorting to what reasoning have you decided to abandon him? Has your mind perhaps been deranged by grief — have you lost your senses?

sanskrit: kunty uvāca yudhiṣṭhira na saṃtāpaḥ kāryaḥ prati vṛkodaram na cāyaṃ buddhidaurbalyād vyavasāyaḥ kṛto mayā
english: Kuntī said: Yudhiṣṭhira, you must have no anguish regarding Vṛkodara — nor has this resolve been made by me out of weakness of mind.

sanskrit: iha viprasya bhavane vayaṃ putra sukhoṣitāḥ tasya pratikriyā tāta mayeyaṃ prasamīkṣitā etāvān eva puruṣaḥ kṛtaṃ yasmin na naśyati
english: Here in the brahmin's house, my son, we have dwelt in comfort; this repayment to him has been carefully considered by me. Only so great a person is one in whom a good deed is not lost.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasya vikrāntaṃ tadā jatugṛhe mahat hiḍimbasya vadhāc caiva viśvāso me vṛkodare
english: Having seen Bhīma's great heroism in the house of lac at that time, and also from the slaying of Hiḍimba — my trust in Vṛkodara is firm.

sanskrit: bāhvor balaṃ hi bhīmasya nāgāyutasamaṃ mahat yena yūyaṃ gajaprakhyā nirvyūḍhā vāraṇāvatāt
english: For the strength of Bhīma's arms is great — equal to ten thousand elephants — by which you, resembling great elephants yourselves, were carried out from Vāraṇāvata.

sanskrit: vṛkodarabalo nānyo na bhūto na bhaviṣyati yo 'bhyudīyād yudhi śreṣṭham api vajradharaṃ svayam
english: There is no other equal to Vṛkodara in strength — there has been none, nor shall there be — who could rise against even the greatest in battle, even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.

sanskrit: jātamātraḥ purā caiṣa mamāṅkāt patito girau śarīragauravāt tasya śilā gātrair vicūrṇitā
english: Long ago, when he was just born, he fell from my lap onto a mountain — because of the heaviness of his body, the rock was shattered by his limbs.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ prajñayā smṛtvā balaṃ bhīmasya pāṇḍava pratīkāraṃ ca viprasya tataḥ kṛtavatī matim
english: Recalling that, O Pāṇḍava, with discernment — Bhīma's strength — and also the brahmin's need for repayment, I then formed this resolve.

sanskrit: nedaṃ lobhān na cājñānān na ca mohād viniścitam buddhipūrvaṃ tu dharmasya vyavasāyaḥ kṛto mayā
english: This was not decided out of greed, nor out of ignorance, nor out of delusion — my effort for dharma has been undertaken with full deliberation.

sanskrit: arthau dvāv api niṣpannau yudhiṣṭhira bhaviṣyataḥ pratīkāraś ca vāsasya dharmaś ca carito mahān
english: Two purposes will both be accomplished, Yudhiṣṭhira: repayment for our lodging, and the practice of great dharma.

sanskrit: yo brāhmaṇasya sāhāyyaṃ kuryād artheṣu karhi cit kṣatriyaḥ sa śubhāṃl lokān prāpnuyād iti me śrutam
english: "A kṣatriya who ever renders assistance to a brahmin in his needs attains auspicious worlds" — thus have I heard.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyasyaiva kurvāṇo vadhamokṣaṇam vipulāṃ kīrtim āpnoti loke 'smiṃś ca paratra ca
english: A kṣatriya who brings about the liberation from death even of another kṣatriya alone wins great fame in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: vaiśyasyaiva tu sāhāyyaṃ kurvāṇaḥ kṣatriyo yudhi sa sarveṣv api lokeṣu prajā rañjayate dhruvam
english: And a kṣatriya who renders assistance even to a vaiśya in battle will assuredly delight the people in all the worlds.

sanskrit: śūdraṃ tu mokṣayan rājā śaraṇārthinam āgatam prāpnotīha kule janma sadravye rājasatkṛte
english: And a king who saves a śūdra who has come seeking refuge — he gains birth here in a family that is prosperous and honoured by kings.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavān vyāsaḥ purā kauravanandana provāca sutarāṃ prājñas tasmād etac cikīrṣitam
english: So the blessed Vyāsa, that wise man, declared this very clearly long ago, O joy of the Kuru line — therefore this is what I intend to do.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca upapannam idaṃ mātas tvayā yad buddhipūrvakam ārtasya brāhmaṇasyaivam anukrośād idaṃ kṛtam dhruvam eṣyati bhīmo 'yaṃ nihatya puruṣādakam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This is fitting, mother — what you have done with full deliberation, out of compassion for a brahmin in distress. Bhīma will certainly return after slaying the man-eater.

sanskrit: yathā tv idaṃ na vindeyur narā nagaravāsinaḥ tathāyaṃ brāhmaṇo vācyaḥ parigrāhyaś ca yatnataḥ
english: But the brahmin must be instructed and carefully persuaded in such a way that the townspeople do not come to know of this.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyām annam ādāya pāṇḍavaḥ bhīmaseno yayau tatra yatrāsau puruṣādakaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then, when the night had passed, the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena took the food and went to the place where that man-eater dwelt.

sanskrit: āsādya tu vanaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ pāṇḍavo balī ājuhāva tato nāmnā tadannam upayojayan
english: And having reached the forest of that demon, the mighty Pāṇḍava called out to him by name, helping himself to the food.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rākṣasaḥ śrutvā bhīmasenasya tad vacaḥ ājagāma susaṃkruddho yatra bhīmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Then that demon, hearing Bhīmasena's words, came in a great rage to where Bhīma stood.

sanskrit: mahākāyo mahāvego dārayann iva medinīm triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ kṛtvā saṃdaśya daśanacchadam
english: Huge-bodied and of immense speed, seeming to cleave the earth, having drawn his brows into a three-peaked frown and biting his lip —

sanskrit: bhuñjānam annaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ vivṛtya nayane kruddha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: — seeing Bhīmasena eating the food, that demon, furious, opened wide his eyes and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ko 'yam annam idaṃ bhuṅkte madartham upakalpitam paśyato mama durbuddhir yiyāsur yamasādanam
english: "Who is this fool of corrupt mind who eats this food prepared for me, before my very eyes — who wishes to go to the abode of Yama?"

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu tac chrutvā prahasann iva bhārata rākṣasaṃ tam anādṛtya bhuṅkta eva parāṅmukhaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, hearing that, O Bhārata, as if laughing, paid no heed to that demon and ate on, turning his back to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhairavaṃ kṛtvā samudyamya karāv ubhau abhyadravad bhīmasenaṃ jighāṃsuḥ puruṣādakaḥ
english: Then, raising both his arms and uttering a terrible roar, that man-eater charged at Bhīmasena, intending to kill him.

sanskrit: tathāpi paribhūyainaṃ nekṣamāṇo vṛkodaraḥ rākṣasaṃ bhuṅkta evānnaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ paravīrahā
english: Even then, utterly disregarding him and not looking at the demon, Vṛkodara, the Pāṇḍava, slayer of enemy heroes, simply went on eating the food.

sanskrit: amarṣeṇa tu saṃpūrṇaḥ kuntīputrasya rākṣasaḥ jaghāna pṛṣṭhaṃ pāṇibhyām ubhābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Filled with wrath, the demon stood behind Kuntī's son and struck him on the back with both his palms.

sanskrit: tathā balavatā bhīmaḥ pāṇibhyāṃ bhṛśam āhataḥ naivāvalokayām āsa rākṣasaṃ bhuṅkta eva saḥ
english: Though struck hard on the back by that powerful being with his palms, Bhīma did not even glance at the demon — he simply went on eating.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhūyaḥ saṃkruddho vṛkṣam ādāya rākṣasaḥ tāḍayiṣyaṃs tadā bhīmaṃ punar abhyadravad balī
english: Then, enraged still further, that mighty demon seized a tree and charged at Bhīma again, intending to strike him.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaḥ śanair bhuktvā tadannaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ vāry upaspṛśya saṃhṛṣṭas tasthau yudhi mahābalaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, that bull among men, finished eating the food at his leisure, sipped water, and stood up in the field of battle, greatly pleased — that mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: kṣiptaṃ kruddhena taṃ vṛkṣaṃ pratijagrāha vīryavān savyena pāṇinā bhīmaḥ prahasann iva bhārata
english: The valiant Bhīma caught the tree hurled by the enraged demon with his left hand, as if laughing, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa punar udyamya vṛkṣān bahuvidhān balī prāhiṇod bhīmasenāya tasmai bhīmaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then that mighty one lifted up many more trees of various kinds and flung them at Bhīmasena — and the Pāṇḍava Bhīma flung them back at him.

sanskrit: tad vṛkṣayuddham abhavan mahīruhavināśanam ghorarūpaṃ mahārāja bakapāṇḍavayor mahat
english: That battle of trees — great, terrible in form, devastating to the forest — took place between Baka and the Pāṇḍava, O great king.

sanskrit: nāma viśrāvya tu bakaḥ samabhidrutya pāṇḍavam bhujābhyāṃ parijagrāha bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: Then Baka, shouting his name aloud, rushed at the Pāṇḍava and seized mighty Bhīmasena with both his arms.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi tad rakṣaḥ parirabhya mahābhujaḥ visphurantaṃ mahāvegaṃ vicakarṣa balād balī
english: And Bhīmasena too, great-armed and mighty, threw his arms around that demon and, as he struggled with great force, dragged him away by sheer power.

sanskrit: sa kṛṣyamāṇo bhīmena karṣamāṇaś ca pāṇḍavam samayujyata tīvreṇa śrameṇa puruṣādakaḥ
english: Dragged by Bhīma and dragging the Pāṇḍava in turn, that man-eater was overcome by extreme exhaustion.

sanskrit: tayor vegena mahatā pṛthivī samakampata pādapāṃś ca mahākāyāṃś cūrṇayām āsatus tadā
english: By their great force the earth trembled, and they pulverised the mighty trees standing around them.

sanskrit: hīyamānaṃ tu tad rakṣaḥ samīkṣya bharatarṣabha niṣpiṣya bhūmau pāṇibhyāṃ samājaghne vṛkodaraḥ
english: But seeing that demon weakening, O bull of the Bharatas, Vṛkodara pressed him down onto the ground with both his hands and struck him.
